fields.description:
Implement CSV export for a report identified by the reportctl --report option. A report ID identifies a report in the server API. The export succeeds when the client downloads a CSV file.

A receipt is the server-issued export identifier. Clients MUST retain the receipt until the download completes unless the user cancels the export.

Clients SHOULD retry failed downloads, except when access has been revoked. Use the existing client retry policy.

See [the API guide](https://example.invalid/api).

Example invocation (report ID 42):

```sh
reportctl export --report 42 --format csv
```

fields.summary: Make the reportctl retry instructions clearer
fields.description:
Update the reportctl CLI retry instructions. Do not change client behavior. A receipt is the server-issued export identifier.

In order to be able to check the export status, it is necessary for you to read the receipt.

The export may have failed. Check its status before retrying.

When the user cancels an export after the server creates a receipt but before the client completes the download, the client MUST NOT automatically delete that receipt unless the server confirms that no retry can still reference it.

Example command for the existing retry behavior:

```sh
reportctl retry --receipt R42
```
Add CSV export. Keep the receipt until the export finishes. A receipt is the server-issued export identifier.
